summary: This resolution impeaches Defense Secretary Peter B. Hegseth and sends six articles of high crimes and misdemeanors to the Senate for trial, alleging he launched unauthorized hostilities against Iran, violated the laws of armed conflict, mishandled classified information on unsecured apps, obstructed congressional oversight, abused his office for political retribution, and undermined military cohesion through discriminatory policies.

The resolution addresses only impeachment articles concerning military operations, information handling, and personnel conduct. No tax policy, rates, or revenue measures are mentioned or implicated.

No provisions address healthcare systems, coverage, or markets. A passing reference to reproductive care appears only as one element of alleged misconduct, without establishing or altering any healthcare policy.

No content relates to immigration, border policy, visas, or enforcement.

One subparagraph criticizes the Secretary for restricting reproductive care access within the military. This is cited solely as evidence of misconduct warranting impeachment and does not enact, expand, or restrict abortion policy.
